title: Degree-zero inclusion of the twisted action site is cocontinuous
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site with pullbacks, s a site autoequivalence continuous in both directions, R a sheaf of commutative rings and a its specified inverse-translation ring isomorphism. For any Site S [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data], the degree-zero inclusion S.inclusion is cocontinuous from J to S.topology: for every object X of C and every S.topology-covering sieve V on S.inclusion.obj X, its functor pullback along S.inclusion is J-covering on X. This is only a covering-sieve property; it asserts no module or tensor comparison.

source.place: proposition-sheaves-on-group (00W0), motivation for the twisted generated-topology argument; cover-lifting substep in step 1 of lem-sf-twisted-action-tensor-comparisons and step 2 of lem-sf-twisted-action-site-core. Agent-formulated twisted variant, not a claim that 00W0 states the twisted result.

proof.text: A generating sieve is the image of an old covering sieve along the degree-zero inclusion. Pullbacks along degree-zero arrows have old covering refinements by the base topology pullback axiom. For an integer-labelled arrow, translate by its integer degree and use the arrow-composition formula to reduce to the degree-zero case. Continuity of both directions of the equivalence implies cover preservation by all its integer powers. Thus each such pullback has a covering degree-zero refinement.

The sieves whose pullbacks along all arrows into their target have covering degree-zero restrictions form a Grothendieck topology: top is immediate, pullback stability reindexes the arrows, and transitivity is the base topology transitivity applied to the covering degree-zero refinement. The first step places all generating sieves in that topology, so S.topology_eq places the generated topology below it. Apply this comparison to a covering sieve and the identity arrow. Empty sites give a vacuous assertion.

mathlib_searches.results: RestrictionPresentation supplies continuity of the inclusion, not cocontinuity. The generated topology and integer-arrow presentation provide the argument but no existing declaration closes this cover-lifting step. Read TwistedActionSiteCore.siteCore: it asserts existence of one cocontinuous Site, which does not supply cocontinuity for an arbitrary Site S in the assigned theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem inclusion_cocontinuous
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (s : C ≌ C)
    [s.functor.IsContinuous J J] [s.inverse.IsContinuous J J]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (a : (s.inverse.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u} J J).obj R ≅ R)
    (S : Site J s R a) :
    letI := S.category
    S.inclusion.IsCocontinuous J S.topology
